title: Markets: Wednesday 4 November

morning.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · before the 10:00 open
summary: Brent swung between about US$107 and below US$101 on reports of US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island and on mediation headlines, then settled 1% lower at US$103.60 ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/oil-prices-climb-after-us-reportedly-strikes-irans-qeshm-island.html); [ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/asx-markets-business-live-news-nov-4/107343406)), its lowest close since 7 October ([Reuters via Global Banking & Finance](https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/oil-rises-report-us-strike-irans-qeshm-island/)). The Nasdaq rose 0.8% on Tuesday as chipmakers rebounded, while Apple fell on a weaker margin forecast and the Dow slipped 0.4%, according to preliminary closing data ([Reuters via StreetInsider](https://www.streetinsider.com/General+News/S%26P+500%2C+Nasdaq+rise+as+tech+stocks+gain+ahead+of+midterm+results/27276330.html)).

S&P/ASX 200 futures were down 22 points (0.3%) to 8,875 near 6am AEDT, after the index rose 0.3% to 8,886.8 on Tuesday (snapshot; [AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-slip-oil-drops-chipmakers-gain-20261104-p61b4s)). The 4.85% cash rate takes effect today; Macquarie is the only major lender so far to confirm it will pass on the full rise.

The first US midterm polls close at 10am AEDT, with some races possibly taking days to call ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/midterm-elections-2026-live-updates.html)); options on the S&P 500 priced a move of about 0.8% either way for Wednesday, according to ORATS data cited by Reuters ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/investors-ready-for-possible-shakeup-in-congress-as-election-day-arrives-4994181)). ABS household spending for September is due at 11:30am.

cards.headline: Brent swings US$6 in a session, then settles at a four-week low
cards.takeaway: Reports of US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island lifted Brent towards US$107 before mediation headlines pulled it below US$101; it settled at US$103.60, the lowest close since 7 October.
cards.key_figure: Brent settle US$103.60 (−US$1.17, −1%), 3 Nov (CNBC) · US$104.36 futures at 7.29am AEDT (snapshot)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's close edition covered the first Qeshm reports. New: the full US-session settle, the intraday range, and Iran's statement that the US response to its demands was not "satisfactory".
cards.what_happened: Brent settled down US$1.17 at US$103.60 and WTI down 37 cents at US$96.09, ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/oil-prices-climb-after-us-reportedly-strikes-irans-qeshm-island.html); [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/economy/oil-prices-extend-losses-as-hopes-grow-for-us-iran-deal/4110398)). Those were Brent's lowest close since 7 October and WTI's since 14 October ([Reuters via Global Banking & Finance](https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/oil-rises-report-us-strike-irans-qeshm-island/)). NAB said Brent traded up towards US$107, fell below US$101, then settled near US$103.7 after the Wall Street Journal reported the strikes ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/asx-markets-business-live-news-nov-4/107343406)). US officials told the Wall Street Journal the US had carried out "limited strikes" ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/oil-prices-climb-after-us-reportedly-strikes-irans-qeshm-island.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari said Qatar is seeking an interim agreement but has no breakthrough to announce, and a senior Iranian official said the sides remain "still far from a deal" (Anadolu; Reuters). Fuel is the main swing factor in the RBA's inflation forecasts.
cards.market_reaction: Brent futures US$104.36 at 7.29am AEDT (snapshot). Gold futures −0.9% to US$3,932.5 (snapshot).
cards.what_to_watch: Any response from Tehran to the latest US proposals; US crude inventory data on Thursday morning Sydney time.

competing_views.view: It is "probably too early to think escalation risks have passed".
Attributes the sell-off to optimism on signs of diplomacy, pared after Iran's "not satisfactory" comment.

cards.headline: Nasdaq rises 0.8% as chipmakers rebound before midterm results
cards.takeaway: The Nasdaq gained 0.8% and the S&P 500 0.35% as Nvidia and AMD bounced, while the Dow fell 0.4%; the Nasdaq-100 remains in correction.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's issue covered Monday's tech sell-off. New: Tuesday's rebound in chipmakers and the preliminary close.
cards.what_happened: According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 rose 0.35% to 7,568.05, the Nasdaq Composite 0.83% to 25,365.67, and the Dow fell 0.40% to 51,782.29 ([Reuters via StreetInsider](https://www.streetinsider.com/General+News/S%26P+500%2C+Nasdaq+rise+as+tech+stocks+gain+ahead+of+midterm+results/27276330.html)). Nvidia and AMD rose about 3% and 5% in afternoon trade, AMD ahead of its results after the bell ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/micron-nvidia-amd-lead-chip-stocks-rebound-140538628.html)). The Philadelphia semiconductor index climbed almost 3% ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-slip-oil-drops-chipmakers-gain-20261104-p61b4s)). The Nasdaq-100 ended Monday more than 10% below its 6 October record close (Reuters).
cards.why_it_matters: ASX technology stocks have tended to follow the US AI trade in recent sessions. The VIX fell about 2% in the session as oil eased ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/asx-markets-business-live-news-nov-4/107343406)).
cards.market_reaction: Tuesday's closing figures are Reuters' preliminary data, published after the 7.30am snapshot; the snapshot tiles still show Monday's closes (S&P 500 7,541.4, −0.5%; Nasdaq 25,164.3, −1.1%; VIX 21.15).
cards.what_to_watch: AMD's results and after-hours move; Apple and AMD set the tone for the AI hardware trade.

cards.headline: Apple shares fall as memory costs squeeze its holiday-quarter margin
cards.takeaway: Apple guided December-quarter gross margin to 45% to 46%, below the 46.3% analyst average, citing memory prices it expects to rise further.
cards.key_figure: December-quarter gross margin guidance 45%–46% vs 46.3% LSEG average estimate
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's close edition had Apple down about 3% after hours. New: the regular-session fall and management's comments on memory supply.
cards.what_happened: Apple beat revenue and earnings estimates for the September quarter, but CFO Kevan Parekh guided December-quarter gross margin to 45% to 46%, mainly because of higher memory costs and Siri AI costs ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/apple-earnings-john-ternus-faces-first-test-amid-high-memory-costs.html)). CEO John Ternus called memory pricing "unprecedented" and predicted December-quarter memory costs would be higher than the September quarters ([The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/02/apple-third-quarter-revenue-earnings)).
cards.why_it_matters: Apple said memory will constrain iPhone and Mac supply in the holiday quarter, as AI server buyers absorb supply (CNBC). That is a cost pressure for hardware makers and a pricing tailwind for memory producers.
cards.market_reaction: Apple fell 3% in morning trade (CNBC) and ended lower after the regular session (Reuters via StreetInsider).

cards.headline: ASX set to open slightly lower ahead of US results
cards.takeaway: Futures point to a 0.3% fall after Tuesday's 0.3% gain, with the Australian dollar easing to about 69.7 US cents.
cards.what_happened: S&P/ASX 200 futures were down 22 points to 8,875 near 6am AEDT ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-slip-oil-drops-chipmakers-gain-20261104-p61b4s)). The ASX 200 rose 30.3 points (0.3%) to 8,886.8 on Tuesday (snapshot).
cards.why_it_matters: The midterm count runs through the ASX session, with the first polls closing at 10am AEDT. Cheaper oil helps airlines and travel stocks, while the lower oil price is a headwind for energy producers.
cards.market_reaction: The Australian dollar eased to near 69.7 US cents ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/asx-markets-business-live-news-nov-4/107343406)); the RBA's 4pm fix on Tuesday was 0.6976, −0.67% (snapshot).
cards.what_to_watch: ABS household spending and job vacancies at 11:30am AEDT.

cards.headline: Big four banks yet to say whether they will pass on the rate rise
cards.takeaway: Macquarie has confirmed a 0.25-point rise from 19 November; none of the big four had announced a change as of 3 November, and ANZ says its rates are under review.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's close covered Macquarie's move. New: the big four had not announced changes by Tuesday evening, and AMP's household-buffer survey.
cards.what_happened: As of 3 November, CBA, Westpac, ANZ and NAB had not announced how they would pass on the 0.25-point rise ([Savings.com.au](https://www.savings.com.au/news/rba-hikes-again-here-s-how-the-big-four-responded); [Nine](https://www.nine.com.au/australia-news/banks-respond-rba-interest-rate-rise-20261103-p61b3u.html)). ANZ's rate-change page says it is reviewing its home loan rates ([ANZ](https://www.anz.com.au/personal/home-loans/interest-rates/rate-changes/)). An AMP survey found 17% of respondents could cover essential expenses for less than a week if their income stopped ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/asx-markets-business-live-news-nov-4/107343406)).
cards.why_it_matters: Bank decisions set how fast the rise reaches household budgets. NAB reports full-year results on Thursday at 10.30am AEDT ([NAB](https://www.nab.com.au/about-us/shareholder-centre/financial-calendar)), giving the first bank commentary after the decision.
cards.what_to_watch: Big four announcements; NAB results on Thursday.

cards.headline: Economists see the RBA on hold after its split-vote rise
cards.takeaway: CommBank now expects the cash rate to stay at 4.85% in December and February, while futures put the odds of a December rise at about 10%.
cards.key_figure: Cash rate 4.85% from today (RBA); the snapshot tile still shows 4.60%
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's close covered the decision and MNI's 35% February pricing. New: CommBank's post-decision call and Market Index's futures reading.
cards.what_happened: CommBank's Belinda Allen said the RBA would "ultimately keep rates on hold" but that the risk of further tightening in 2027 remains ([CommBank](https://www.commbank.com.au/articles/newsroom/2026/11/commbank-november-rba-cash-rate-increase-analysis.html)). ASX 30-day cash rate futures put the chance of a December rise at about 10% in early trade after the decision ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/rba-hikes-interest-rate-to-4-85-but-a-split-vote-hints-the-end-may-be-near)).
cards.why_it_matters: The RBA forecasts headline inflation peaking at 4.5% in the December quarter and headline inflation above 3% until late 2027 ([RBA SMP](https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/smp/2026/nov/pdf/statement-on-monetary-policy-2026-11.pdf)). The October monthly CPI on 25 November is the next test.

competing_views.view: Expects holds in December and February, then cuts in August and November 2027.

competing_views.who: UBS (as summarised by Market Index, 28 Oct note)
competing_views.view: Risks skewed to a further rise to 5.10%, most likely in February 2027.

cards.headline: US job openings beat forecasts at 7.5 million; Treasury yields rise
cards.takeaway: September openings came in above forecasts and quits rose, while layoffs were little changed.
cards.key_figure: Job openings 7.523m in September vs a revised 7.2m in August (BLS)
cards.new_since_last_issue: New: September JOLTS data released Tuesday.
cards.what_happened: The BLS said openings were little changed at about 7.5 million (a rate of 4.5%), after August was revised up to 7.2 million; quits increased to 3.4 million and layoffs were little changed at 1.6 million ([BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/jolts.nr0.htm)). The forecast had been about 7.13 million ([Vedainvesting](https://vedainvesting.com/en/economic-calendar-today-3-november-2026/)).
cards.why_it_matters: A firmer labour market supports the case for further Fed tightening. CBA expects two and possibly three Fed rises by March 2027, narrowing Australia's rate advantage and weighing on the Australian dollar ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/asx-markets-business-live-news-nov-4/107343406)).
cards.market_reaction: The US 10-year yield rose more than 5bp to 4.948% and the 2-year more than 2bp to 4.612% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/us-treasury-yields-bonds.html)).
cards.what_to_watch: ISM services and ADP on Thursday morning Sydney time, then October payrolls on Saturday morning Sydney time.

cards.headline: Midterm results arrive through the ASX session
cards.takeaway: Polls show Democrats favoured to take the House with the Senate too close to call; options imply a 0.8% S&P 500 move on Wednesday.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Tuesday's issue covered JPMorgan's scenarios. New: UBS's probabilities, options pricing and poll-closing times.
cards.what_happened: Polls start closing at 6pm ET (10am AEDT) and Alaska finishes around 1am ET (5pm AEDT); some races may take days to call ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/midterm-elections-2026-live-updates.html)). UBS Global Wealth Management puts a Democratic sweep at 50%, a split Congress at 40% and a Republican hold at 10% ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/investors-ready-for-possible-shakeup-in-congress-as-election-day-arrives-4994181)).
cards.why_it_matters: UBS Global Wealth Management CIO Mark Haefele said the most visible effects of a change in control would likely be greater oversight of the administration and more difficult fiscal negotiations; analysts cited by Reuters expect a Democratic sweep to bring investigations into the technology sector (Reuters via Investing.com).

competing_views.view: Equity reaction "likely positive" if Republicans keep the Senate and negative if Democrats gain more Senate seats than expected.
"Election hedges can expire; geopolitical risk doesn't have an expiration date."

cards.headline: Trump says US aid to Israel will stop at year-end; which funding is unclear
cards.takeaway: Trump said about US$4 billion a year in aid would be "cut off at the end of the year", but the current agreement runs to 2028 and Congress has approved funding through September 2027.
cards.what_happened: In a phone interview with "Fox & Friends", Trump said he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "made a deal months ago" and that the money would get "cut off at the end of the year"; NBC News said it was not immediately clear which funding he meant ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/trump-says-us-will-stop-4b-military-aid-israel-end-2026-rcna607210)). Netanyahu's office declined to comment (NBC News).
cards.why_it_matters: The 2016 memorandum of understanding sets US$3.8 billion a year and expires in 2028 (NBC News). Congress has already approved funding through September 2027, i24NEWS reported ([i24NEWS](https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/analysis-opinion/artc-trump-announces-end-to-us-aid-to-israel-by-2027-but-can-he-actually-do-it)). Brent fell after the remarks ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-slip-oil-drops-chipmakers-gain-20261104-p61b4s)).
cards.what_to_watch: Any statement from Netanyahu's office or Congress on the 2016 aid agreement.
